value.means: One row per sales line — all 223,974 of them, ten years of orders from 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, both the physical shops and the web shop — carrying what the customer was actually charged for that line after discount, in US dollars. The "conversion" is an identity: nothing was multiplied or divided, because the money on these rows is recorded in USD already and the currency code beside it says only what the customer transacted in. The alternative reading, treating each amount as local money and converting it at that sale's own order-date rate, was computed and is 219,837,055.56 — 1,022,583.90 higher, 0.47% — and I am not using it, because the declarations state these amounts are USD and expressly forbid this rate as a way to produce USD.

SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS lines_matched,
  SUM(s.net_amount) AS net_usd_as_declared,
  SUM(s.net_amount / f.rate) AS net_if_amounts_were_local_converted_to_usd,
  SUM(s.net_amount * f.rate) AS net_if_multiplied_by_rate,
  MIN(f.rate) AS min_rate,
  MAX(f.rate) AS max_rate
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
JOIN contoso_served.v_contoso5_fx_rate AS f
  ON s.order_date = f.date_day
  AND s.currency_code = f.to_currency
  AND f.from_currency = 'USD'
